summary: On a long mission, the nearest doctor can be minutes away by radio, so astronauts have to watch their own health. VitalOrbit helps with that. It pulls together wearable, checkup, dosimeter, mood and camera data (all simulated in this prototype) and gives each reading a green, yellow or red status. Every status comes with a short explanation and steps that only use the on-board medical kit. If something turns red, the crew gets alerted right away and a report for the flight surgeon waits on board until the link to Earth comes back. We mapped every indicator to one of NASA’s five hazards of human spaceflight. The whole app can works offline.
details:
The astronaut is the main user. Their screen has a 3D body map you can click, nine indicator cards (heart rate, SpO2, temperature, blood pressure, glucose, sleep, mood, radiation dose, body mass) and a 30 day trend for each one. Pick an indicator and you see why it matters in space, what to do now and when to call for help. Two more views sit next to it. Crew members only see each other’s overall status and emergency alerts, so the detailed readings stay private. The flight surgeon on Earth gets the full history and alert log whenever the link is up.

Behind this is a simple rule engine that checks thresholds and trends. Three nights in a row under 6 hours of sleep turns red. A resting heart rate that keeps rising for 5 days turns yellow, even if today’s number looks fine. The radiation limit changes with the mission profile you pick (ISS, Moon, Mars or rover). A yellow alert stays with the astronaut. A red one goes to the crew and gets queued for Earth.

We also built a camera safety check. It runs MediaPipe body, hand and face tracking inside the browser. If someone stays completely still for too long, the app asks “Are you OK?”, and if nobody answers it raises a red alert. Video never leaves the device. A separate spine check flags posture issues, but only as a cue, not a diagnosis.

Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Recharts, Three.js and MediaPipe. An optional Fastify and WebSocket server syncs alerts live between devices for the demo.

Next, we want to connect real wearables, learn a personal baseline for each crew member, and add microscope image analysis and on-board virus sequencing.
